reason: The cited evidence (E1-E6) is drawn entirely from a single paper that directly reports the fabrication, characterization, and 1400 °C oxidation testing of Hf-Al2O3 co-doped MoSi2 coatings, confirming the formation of (Mo,Hf)Si2-Al2O3, the development of an HfO2-SiO2-mullite scale, and reduced mass gain. The premises are therefore fully supported by accurately represented experimental results from that study.
premises: Hf and Al2O3 can be co-doped into a MoSi2 coating
The co-doped coating forms a protective oxide scale containing HfO2, SiO2, and mullite at 1400 °C
This oxide scale acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier, reducing oxidation rate
The co-doped coating shows reduced mass gain compared to undoped MoSi2 after 40 h at 1400 °C
The coating is effective at 1400 °C in static air
